subject: SLA alignment for CloudRidge launch — uptime & credits
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudridge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudridge.com
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SLA alignment for CloudRidge launch — uptime & credits

Karthik —

Thanks for the product demo yesterday. We're preparing a go-live plan for CloudRidge's AI assistant (targeting first customers in March) and need to align on SLA terms before procurement signs off. High-level asks from our side: 

- Hosted availability target: 99.95% (monthly) for the initial launch window (first 90 days)
- Monthly service credits capped at 5-10% (we prefer lower cap but want meaningful remediation)
- P99 latency objective: 150ms for generation calls (we understand bursty patterns)
- Maintenance carveouts: we'd accept planned windows if notified in advance (preferably 72 hours)

Can you share your standard SLA and a proposed credit calculation? Also, please let me know if Redwood can temporarily bump hosted availability for the pilot or whether we should move to a Dedicated reservation to get 99.95.

Thanks —
Samantha Li
Director, CloudOps
CloudRidge
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA alignment for CloudRidge launch — uptime & credits

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks and congrats on the fast timeline. I've looped in Laura (sales lead) and Marissa (Customer Success) so we can align commercial and operational sides. Quick answers up front:

- Our standard Hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly availability. Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers can contract for 99.95% with a higher commitment level.
- Standard credit calculation is proportional to downtime minutes per month; we typically cap cumulative credits at a percentage of the monthly invoice (standard hosted cap: 10%).
- Latency objectives are typically published as targets (p50/p95/p99) but not part of financial remedy for hosted plans. For Dedicated we can discuss tighter latency guardrails if coupled with a sizing/throughput commitment.

That said, we can be flexible for pilots. I'm attaching a tailored draft SLA and a credit matrix with two options: (1) temporary hosted exception to 99.95 for a fixed 90-day pilot with a graduated credit cap; (2) Dedicated baseline terms. Please review and tell me which direction you'd prefer.

Attachments: SLA-draft-cloudridge-v2.pdf, uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx

Proposed next steps:
- Samantha: indicate preference (hosted pilot vs dedicated)
- If hosted pilot: we propose a 90-day exception with an agreed credit cap schedule and a maintenance notification clause
- We'll route the final redlines to legal once commercial is agreed

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudridge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cloudridge.com
Date: 2026-02-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA alignment for CloudRidge launch — uptime & credits

Karthik —

Thanks — reviewed the attachments. A few clarifications and counter-proposals: 

- We'd prefer to remain on Hosted to avoid procurement complexity; so the hosted-pilot exception is our first choice.
- For the 90-day pilot we can accept a temporary exception to 99.95, but we need the monthly credit cap to be meaningful: propose 5% cap Month 1 (to limit vendor risk), 7.5% Month 2 if we see instability, and revert to standard hosted 10% cap only if there's a sustained issue.
- We need p99 latency called out as an objective and included in your monitoring dashboard for joint review; not requesting financial credits tied to latency at this time, but we want visibility and an SLA reporting cadence (weekly for first month, then biweekly).
- Maintenance: 72-hour advance notice is fine; we also require a short emergency-maintenance notification process + on-call escalation path during launch.

I'll circulate this internally and aim to get procurement feedback by end of day Thursday.

Samantha
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T08:38:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: CloudRidge SLA playbook

Karthik/Marissa —

Quick internal note on negotiation posture before we reply:

- We should be willing to offer a timeboxed hosted pilot at 99.95 for 90 days to win the account. Market signals show pilots convert higher if we remove the Dedicated friction.
- Counter on credit caps: suggest a middle ground — Month 1: 7.5% cap, Month 2–3: 5% cap, then default back to standard hosted (10%) or transition to Dedicated. This gives CloudRidge tangible remedy while limiting our exposure.
- Include a clear SLA reporting cadence and an escalation path (CS + Eng on-call) with guaranteed response SLAs for severity P1/P2 during the pilot window.
- Legal: ask for expedited review on the maintenance carveouts and the emergency-notification language.

I'll prepare language to include in the next outbound. Agree we should push for a renewal hook (if they stay past 90 days, migrate to Dedicated pricing or longer-term hosted commitment).

- Laura
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-23T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: 90-day hosted pilot / SLA terms (CloudRidge)

Samantha —

Per our internal alignment, here's a consolidated proposal for the launch pilot. If this looks good we'll push to DocuSign and legal will do a quick redline pass: 

Summary: 90-day Hosted Pilot at temporary availability target 99.95% (monthly)
- Credit cap schedule (as % of monthly invoice):
  - Month 1: 7.5% cap
  - Month 2–3: 5% cap
  - After pilot: default Hosted cap 10% unless we transition to Dedicated terms
- Credit calculation: credits issued proportional to total downtime minutes below target, per the attached uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx (standard methodology in the draft SLA)
- Monitoring & reporting: weekly SLA report (first 4 weeks), then biweekly for remainder of pilot. Dashboard access will be provided to CloudRidge ops.
- Latency: p99 generation objective 150ms (operational objective only). We will include p50/p95/p99 charts in the SLA reports; latency will not be a financial remedy for Hosted during pilot.
- Maintenance & emergency ops:
  - Planned maintenance: 72-hour advance notice, standard carveouts apply
  - Emergency maintenance: Redwood will provide as-early-as-possible notice and an escalation path; during the pilot we commit to a P1 response acknowledgement within 30 minutes and on-call engagement until mitigation

Attachments: SLA-draft-cloudridge-v2.pdf, uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/CRG-SLA-88921

Would you be able to confirm CloudRidge acceptance of the schedule above by EOD Wednesday so we can start legal review?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudridge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cloudridge.com
Date: 2026-02-24T15:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 90-day hosted pilot / SLA terms (CloudRidge)

Karthik —

Thanks, this is mostly aligned and appreciated the pragmatic approach. We are prepared to accept the 90-day hosted pilot and the credit schedule you laid out, subject to two small additions: 

1) Emergency maintenance clause: please add explicit 72-hour escalation window for high-severity incidents where we can request an incident post-mortem within 48 hours of mitigation.
2) Notification: require that planned maintenance impacting >1% of capacity trigger an ops-level heads-up and a Go/No-Go check 24 hours prior to execution.

If you can add those two bullets into the SLA doc and send a DocuSign version, we'll route the signature. We also want to add our account exec (will share the name in a follow-up) to the final envelope.

Samantha Li
Director, CloudOps
CloudRidge
